headline: Am I being deceived?
note:
🔄 REWRITTEN 2026-08-19 to the Natural Tarot-Cut framework. Bubbles 3-6 run as ONE causal chain — so / and / but / that's why — and the read ANSWERS. The art line and the bridge are unchanged. Every ban in this note still stands.

Face-down only (return-mhf). 🔴 NO VERDICT IN EITHER DIRECTION. These three name an untruth outright, so both answers are live harms: 'he lied to you' is an accusation against a real man on no evidence, and 'he is telling you the truth' is a reassurance the funnel has no standing to give — and on this audience the second is the more dangerous of the two. 🔴 Never blame her judgment: naive, gullible, too trusting, 'should have known' are all out. 🔴 No timeframe.

Finding: 'deceived' is a heavier word than 'lied to' — it means a whole picture, not one sentence. She is asking whether the shape of the thing is what she thinks. ⚠️ Its beat 2 could not restate her headline: 'you are being deceived' is itself a banned phrase, so the echo is built as 'you asked about being deceived'.

a: You turned the Magician, dear. Look — his right arm is straight up and quite still.
You asked about being deceived. Your hand went to the man who sets a whole scene.
So deceived is a big word, dear. It means the whole picture.
And he sets out all of it himself, dear. Every piece.
But a whole picture is harder to check than one line, dear.
That's why nothing pins down, dear. You're checking it all at once.
Let me look closer at what has been arranged around you…
b: You turned the Hanged Man, dear. Look — the wood he hangs from is a single cut beam.
You asked about being deceived. Your hand went to the card that turns a whole picture over.
So you've been trying to turn the whole thing over, dear.
And there's one view of him, dear, and no way to walk round it.
But the shape of what you can't see isn't mine to give, dear.
That's why the not-seeing has worn you down. You've carried it alone, dear.
Let me look closer at what has been keeping this side-on to you…
c: You turned the Fool, dear. Look — his tunic is patterned all over with small shapes.
You asked about being deceived. Your hand went to the one who wears no disguise.
So one odd piece doesn't tell you the whole design, dear.
And his coat has many small shapes, dear, and only one pattern.
But you've been holding the pieces up one at a time, dear.
That's why nothing has come together yet, dear. You were right to look.
Let me look closer at what has been holding the pattern out of view…
